events.event: PHP Foundation releases security fixes for two critical 'php2shell' flaws in the PHP core, found with AI by Wiz and Calif researchers, after details leaked; exploitation attempts reportedly climbed to millions and agencies in several countries issued warnings.
events.key_numbers: PHP powers ~70% of websites worldwide (Wiz estimate) · patches released Wed 21 Oct 2026 · Cloudflare exploit attempts: thousands in 10 h before announcement → tens of thousands within 45 min → hundreds of thousands within 2 h → millions · affects WordPress, Laravel, Symfony, Drupal
events.why_it_matters: Most Indonesian websites, from shops to government portals, run on PHP, so owners must update the PHP runtime and users should expect phishing that rides the news.
events.spreading_evidence: Katadata ran 5+ articles on it as featured items; CNN Indonesia Teknologi headline 22 Oct

events.event: Perpres 27/2026 lets ojol drivers work with more than one app company at once and requires apps to pay drivers' share in real time after each job; the Ministry of MSMEs is designated to oversee partnership agreements.
events.key_numbers: Perpres 27/2026 · Pasal 3(1): driver may partner with one or more platforms · Pasal 12: app fee max 8% (driver keeps 92%, previously 20% cut) · 14 mandatory partnership obligations (not listed) · commission rule effective 1 Jul 2026 per CNBC
events.why_it_matters: Millions of ojol drivers and daily riders are affected by who gets paid how much, and how fast.

events.event: BRIN says the object that fell in a palm-oil plantation near Sampit, Central Kalimantan, is debris from a Chinese rocket (reported as a ZQ-2E), described as car-sized.
events.key_numbers: Debris reportedly car-sized · location: oil-palm plantation near Sampit, Kalteng · rocket model ZQ-2E per detikPedia headline (not verified in article body)
events.why_it_matters: A rocket stage landing on farmland raises who is liable for space debris and how safe it is.

events.event: Anthropic's draft IPO prospectus, per Reuters via CNBC Indonesia, shows a large first-half 2026 net loss, mostly from an accounting charge, alongside fast revenue growth; the IPO is planned for November.
events.key_numbers: H1 2026 net loss US$80 B (~Rp1,449 T) vs US$13 B before · US$72 B of it is a non-cash accounting charge · FY2025 net loss US$42 B · operating loss US$8.1 B on revenue US$4.6 B (period unclear) · Q3 revenue +45% to US$16.8 B · investor valuation talk ~US$1.5 T · IPO planned Nov
events.why_it_matters: Shows how expensive the AI race is, and whether an AI bubble could hit markets and the data-centre boom coming to Indonesia.
events.spreading_evidence: CNBC Indonesia Tech featured headline; detikInet Inet Flash video 21 Oct

events.event: Data-centre buyers drive Puradelta Lestari (DMAS) land sales at Kota Deltamas, Cikarang, with Microsoft Operations Indonesia the biggest buyer.
events.key_numbers: As of 30 Sep 2026: Microsoft Rp795.96 B (30.06%) · Digital Gayana Ekagrata Rp741.50 B · Princeton Digital Group Rp446.12 B · Indoedge Rp276.06 B · top four ~Rp2.26 T (85.35% of top-buyer list) · 9M 2026 revenue Rp2.65 T (~3.4x y/y) · industrial land Rp2.54 T (~96%)
events.why_it_matters: Shows the AI data-centre boom is already turning into real land deals near Jakarta, with power and water questions attached.

events.event: Apple's Indonesian pre-order for the iPhone Duo is reported to open on 23 Oct 2026 at 09.00 WIB; the price is still unofficial.
events.key_numbers: Pre-order 23 Oct 2026, 09.00 WIB (per detik and several outlets) · leaked/predicted prices Rp43.99 M (256 GB) to Rp68.9 M (top model, prediction) · global price US$1,999
events.why_it_matters: A foldable iPhone costing about the price of a small car is the headline for Indonesian gadget buyers.
events.spreading_evidence: detikInet Gadget News and News Feed headlines; many outlets

events.event: Apple commits up to US$100 million of US-recycled titanium over three years from Perryman Company for the iPhone Duo and other products, under its American Manufacturing Program; CNBC Indonesia's headline frames it as TKDN, although the deal concerns US content.
events.key_numbers: Up to US$100 M (~Rp1.8 T) over 3 years · at least 80% recycled titanium · nearly 100 components from US firms in 12+ states · US$600 B four-year US pledge · TSMC Arizona >100 M chips for Apple in 2026
events.why_it_matters: Useful as a correction: the Rp1.8 T is Apple's US spending, not an Indonesian TKDN obligation.
